items.title: Nick Polites Interview, 1963-10-08
items.q: INTERVIEWER mentions Tom Pickering in the context of Eight Monsborough records; INTERVIEWEE does not mention knowing Tom Pickering personally, only discussing Eight Monsborough.

ctx.x: that in Australia. Never had an all-night rave. Yeah. And what about the jazz conventions? That's an exceptional thing. It's an amateur sort of organisation done by musicians. Once a year, between Christmas and New Year for a week, they meet in one town in Australia. They travel, they travel a thousand miles, some of them. They all get together and every day and night for that week, they play and talk and drink together and have a marvellous time. It's really a wonderful experience. I've been to most of them…

clarinet blues. Yes, yes. And it seems to sell that jazz group, but sometimes they had what, Tom Pickering on clarinet. He's a Tasmanian. Yeah, but I don't know why. But it seems to me that that's one of the things about the clarinet blues. Yes, they used to do it quite a bit more. Yes, they used to do it quite a bit. And of course, you have so much doubling of instruments down there. Like, well,

eight Monsborough is a classic example. Yes. It is really exceptional. It's just that he appears on so many records, I think, that might give you that impression. There isn't really very much doubling, except when eight does it. What all has he played since you've known him? What instruments? Oh, well, every instrument. Every instrument. He's quit the alto. He's changed to tenor. And plays that very well, as he plays most instruments. He was first known as Plunk Monsborough. He used to play banjo. As I say, he's…
